# Porting highlight.js grammars to Swift

This library is a native Swift port of highlight.js 11.11.1 (commit
`08cb242e7d4aee787114eb04cc7ab18314d82f92`). Compare against a checkout of
that revision; no developer-specific reference path is part of the repository.
The engine (`Sources/HighlightKit/Core`) ports `highlight.js` and
`mode_compiler.js`; grammars in `Sources/HighlightKit/Languages` correspond to
`src/languages/<name>.js` in the reference checkout.

**Fidelity is verified mechanically**: reference fixtures are generated by
running the actual highlight.js source (see *Verification loop* below). The
Swift port must produce identical token ranges and scope stacks; relevance is
compared with the test suite's 0.001 numeric tolerance.

## File conventions

- One language per file: `Sources/HighlightKit/Languages/<Name>.swift`
  (capitalized language key, e.g. `Cpp.swift`, `Objectivec.swift`).
- Each file defines:

```swift
import Foundation

extension LanguageCatalog {
    /// C++. Port of highlight.js `languages/cpp.js`.
    public static let cpp = LanguageDescriptor(name: "cpp", aliases: [...]) {
        // build and return LanguageDefinition — a *fresh* tree per call
        ...
    }
}
```

- The factory closure must build a fresh `Mode` tree on every call
  (compilation mutates modes). Use local `let`/`func` helpers exactly
  mirroring the JS source's local `const`s.
- A factory is synchronous and non-reentrant: it must not call a
  `Highlighter`, compile another registered language, or perform highlighting.
  The registry serializes one generation's construction and rejects such
  calls deterministically, even when the requested language is already warm.
- Shared cross-grammar fragments live in `Languages/Lib/`
  (`Ecmascript.swift`, `CssShared.swift`, …) as computed `static var`s
  (fresh instance per access) or `static let` for plain `[String]`
  word lists / pattern strings.
- For a newly bundled language, add its descriptor to
  `Sources/HighlightKit/Languages/LanguageCatalog.swift` and keep the public
  list in a stable, reviewable order. Alias registration is derived from the
  descriptor.

## Mode field mapping (JS → Swift)

| JS | Swift |
|---|---|
| `className: 'x'` / `scope: 'x'` | `scope: "x"` |
| `scope: {1: "a", 3: "b"}` | `scope: [1: "a", 3: "b"]` |
| `className: null` (variant canceling base scope) | `scope: ScopeRef.none` |
| `match: /re/` | `match: "re"` (raw string `#"re"#` recommended) |
| `match: [re1, re2]` | `match: ["re1", "re2"]` |
| `begin:`/`end:` | same; computed patterns need `.re(expr)` |
| `beginScope`/`endScope` | same types as `scope` |
| `beginKeywords: "a b"` | `beginKeywords: "a b"` |
| `keywords: "a b"` | `keywords: "a b"` |
| `keywords: [..]` | `keywords: ["a", "b"]` |
| `keywords: {$pattern, keyword, literal, ...}` | `Keywords(pattern: ..., ["keyword": ..., "literal": ...])` |
| keyword `"word\|10"` relevance | identical (`"word\|10"`) |
| `contains: [...]` | `contains: [...]` |
| `contains: ['self']` | `contains: [Mode.selfReference]` |
| `variants: [...]` | `variants: [...]` |
| `starts: {...}` | `starts: Mode(...)` |
| `subLanguage: 'xml'` | `subLanguage: ["xml"]` |
| `subLanguage: ['a','b']` | `subLanguage: ["a", "b"]` |
| `illegal: /re/` | `illegal: ["re"]` |
| `illegal: [/a/, /b/]` | `illegal: ["a", "b"]` |
| `relevance: n` | `relevance: n` |
| `label: "x"` | `label: "x"` |
| flags (`excludeBegin`, `returnEnd`, `skip`, `endsParent`, `endsWithParent`, …) | identical names |
| `hljs.END_SAME_AS_BEGIN({...})` | `Mode(..., endSameAsBegin: true)` |
| `'on:begin'` / `'on:end'` | `onBegin:` / `onEnd:` (`ModeCallback`) |
| `hljs.inherit(M, {overrides})` | build `M`, then mutate the copy: `{ let m = ...; m.x = y; return m }()` |

**Argument order is fixed** (Swift requires it):
`scope, match, begin, beginScope, beginKeywords, beforeMatch, end,
endScope, endSameAsBegin, keywords, illegal, contains, variants,
starts, subLanguage, relevance, label, excludeBegin, excludeEnd,
returnBegin, returnEnd, skip, endsParent, endsWithParent, onBegin, onEnd`.
Reorder JS keys to match when porting.

`hljs.*` helpers map to `CommonModes.*`:
`C_LINE_COMMENT_MODE → cLineCommentMode`, `C_BLOCK_COMMENT_MODE →
cBlockCommentMode`, `HASH_COMMENT_MODE → hashCommentMode`,
`QUOTE_STRING_MODE → quoteStringMode`, `APOS_STRING_MODE →
aposStringMode`, `BACKSLASH_ESCAPE → backslashEscape`, `NUMBER_MODE /
C_NUMBER_MODE / BINARY_NUMBER_MODE → numberMode / cNumberMode /
binaryNumberMode`, `REGEXP_MODE → regexpMode`, `TITLE_MODE →
titleMode`, `UNDERSCORE_TITLE_MODE → underscoreTitleMode`,
`METHOD_GUARD → methodGuard`, `SHEBANG(...) → shebang(binary:relevance:)`,
`COMMENT(b, e, opts) → comment(b, e) { $0.… }` (the closure applies
`opts`; doctag/english-words children are appended automatically),
`hljs.IDENT_RE → identRe`, `UNDERSCORE_IDENT_RE`, `NUMBER_RE`,
`C_NUMBER_RE`, `BINARY_NUMBER_RE`, `RE_STARTERS_RE`, `MATCH_NOTHING_RE`
(all on `CommonModes`). `hljs.regex.concat/either/lookahead/optional/
anyNumberOfTimes → RegexSource.*` (all take/return `String`).

Language-level:

```swift
LanguageDefinition(
    name: "cpp",                      // registry key
    aliases: [...],                   // same as descriptor
    caseInsensitive: true,            // JS case_insensitive
    classNameAliases: [...:...],      // JS classNameAliases
    disableAutodetect: true,
    supersetOf: "c",
    root: Mode(keywords: ..., illegal: ..., contains: [...])
)
```

`unicodeRegex: true` has no Swift equivalent (ICU is always
Unicode-aware) — just drop it.

## Regex translation (JS → ICU) — the critical part

Patterns are compiled with `NSRegularExpression`
(`.anchorsMatchLines`, plus `.caseInsensitive` for case-insensitive
languages). Most JS patterns work unchanged, **except**:

1. **`[` inside a character class must be escaped**: JS `[{}[\],:]` →
   ICU `[{}\[\],:]`. ICU treats a bare `[` in a class as a *nested
   class*. This is the #1 source of failures — scan every character
   class you port.
2. **`[^]` → `[\s\S]`** (ICU rejects the empty negated class).
3. **JS string-literal escapes**: grammars often write patterns as JS
   *strings*, where `'\.'` is just `'.'` (the backslash vanishes!) but
   `'\\.'` is regex `\.`. Read carefully: `begin: '\.?html`'` is the
   regex `.?html\`` — an *any-char* dot, not a literal dot. Regex
   *literals* (`/…/`) have no such trap. When in doubt check with
   `node -e "console.log('\.?html\`')"`.
4. **Empty pattern strings** (`end: ''`) mean *unset* (JS falsiness).
   The Swift compiler handles `""` as nil — port them as written or
   drop them.
5. `\p{L}` etc. work natively in ICU (no `u` flag needed).
6. ICU rejects some patterns JS accepts (dangling `{`, empty
   alternation in odd places). The compilation test will tell you
   (`swift test --filter GrammarCompilation`), with the failing
   pattern in the message.
7. In Swift, prefer raw strings `#"..."#` so `\s` etc. need no double
   escaping. Use string interpolation for composition:
   `#"\b("# + words + #")\b"#` or `.re(...)` with `RegexSource` helpers.

## Callbacks

```swift
let cb: ModeCallback = { match, response in
    // match[0], match[1]… — group text (nil if group didn't participate)
    // match.index — UTF-16 offset of the match
    // match.input — the full NSString, indexed in UTF-16 units
    // match.precedingUnit — UTF-16 unit before the match
    response.ignoreMatch()
    response.data["key"] = "value"   // carried from this begin to its end
}
```

JS `match.input.substring(...)` etc. → use `match.input` (NSString)
with `NSRange` APIs. Precompile any helper `NSRegularExpression`s
outside the closure with `try!`.

### Variant boolean flags (known limitation)

A `variants` entry can override any *value* field of its base
(`scope`, `begin`, `keywords`, `relevance`, `scope: .none` to cancel a
scope, …) but **cannot flip a boolean flag from `true` back to `false`**
(`excludeBegin`, `returnEnd`, `skip`, `endsParent`, …). In highlight.js's
`inherit` a variant with `excludeBegin: false` overrides a `true` base;
in Swift these are non-optional `Bool` defaulting `false`, so "variant
set false" is indistinguishable from "variant left it unset" — and the
Swift `Mode` initializer cannot even *express* an explicit `false`
override. No bundled grammar relies on this (all 375 fixtures pass), and
it is unreachable from the Swift API, so it is left as documented rather
than modeled with tri-state optionals.

### Keyword-group collisions

JS keyword dicts rely on object insertion order: when a word appears in
several groups (`integer` as both `keyword` and `type` in sql.js), the
*last* group wins at compile time. Swift's `Keywords` groups are
unordered — resolve such collisions in the grammar by removing the word
from the earlier group(s) so the compiled table matches highlight.js
(add a comment noting the dedup). The fidelity fixtures will catch any
you miss (symptom: nondeterministic scope for the colliding word).

## Word lists

Big keyword arrays port as `[String]` literals. Generate them mechanically
from the pinned reference checkout rather than typing them, and include the
reproducible command in the change description. `KEYWORDS.join(' ')` style
usage maps to `Keywords.Group(words: list)` or `.joined(separator: " ")`
where a begin pattern needs the text.

## Verification loop (required)

1. `swift build` — fix compile errors.
2. `swift test --filter GrammarCompilation` — all regexes must compile.
3. Compare seeded inputs against a highlight.js 11.11.1 checkout:

   ```sh
   swift build -c release
   HIGHLIGHTJS_DIR=/path/to/highlight.js \
     python3 Scripts/difftest.py <lang> 1000 1
   ```

   Pass `--reference /path/to/highlight.js` instead of the environment
   variable if preferred. The checked-in harness exits nonzero on reference
   errors or output differences.
4. Add or update paired fixtures under
   `Tests/HighlightKitTests/Fixtures/<lang>/`. This repository does not ship
   a fixture generator; a fixture-changing PR must include or link the
   reviewed generator, pin its highlight.js commit, and record its exact
   invocation. Inputs may be upstream-derived or reviewed adversarial cases,
   but expected token JSON must always be regenerated from the pinned source;
   never hand-edit it merely to make a failure pass.
5. `FIDELITY_LANG=<lang> swift test --filter matchesReference` — every
   fixture must match token-for-token (ranges, scope stacks) and in
   relevance. Iterate until green. Do not weaken the test.
6. Run the full `swift test` to ensure nothing else broke.

Do not delete a failing fixture because a sub-language differs. Identify the
dependency, fix or explicitly document the divergence, and add the smallest
regression case that pins the decision.

## Reference ports to imitate

- `Sources/HighlightKit/Languages/Json.swift` — minimal, beginKeywords,
  illegal.
- `Sources/HighlightKit/Languages/Xml.swift` — variants, starts,
  endsWithParent/endsParent,
  sub-languages, case-insensitive, `\p{L}`.
- `Sources/HighlightKit/Languages/Css.swift` — keywords `$pattern`,
  classNameAliases,
  generated word lists, `hljs.inherit` translation.
- `Sources/HighlightKit/Languages/Javascript.swift` — callbacks, `'self'`,
  multi-match with
  scope maps, labels, cyclic `contains`, `ScopeRef.none`, template
  sub-languages, the JS-string-escape trap.
